items.title: Applied Optoelectronics falls sharply after new $550 million share-sale authorization
items.summary: Applied Optoelectronics entered a new at-the-market agreement allowing sales of up to $550 million in stock. Shares fell in premarket trading despite substantial reported AI optical-networking revenue growth. The agreement permits future sales but does not establish that $550 million has already been issued; capital intensity and dilution remain key risks.

observations.label: November 18 07:10 AM EST premarket observation
observations.value: AAOI -10.6% in pre-open trading (Investing.com); preliminary intraday indication, not a closing price

observations.label: November 17 SEC filing
observations.value: New equity distribution agreement: up to $550 million of common stock, through Raymond James and Needham; discretionary sales, not completed issuance

observations.label: Recent operating context
observations.value: Q3 revenue $269.9 million, approximately +128% year over year, according to November 17 market reporting; substantial capacity capex

observations.label: Risks and invalidation
observations.value: Track actual shares sold, dilution, cash flow, capex returns, optical transceiver orders and margins; improving cash conversion could offset financing concerns

items.key_finding: AI-networking demand growth is accompanied by a material, documented new dilution capacity and negative premarket repricing.

sources.title: Barron's November 18 financing and AI-networking analysis

items.title: Credo and Marvell resolve active electrical cable patent dispute
items.summary: Credo announced an agreement with Marvell over Active Electrical Cable patent rights and pending USPTO challenges. Credo shares rose after hours following the November 17 announcement. This removes a disclosed legal overhang on data-center connectivity, though undisclosed agreement terms prevent assessment of licensing economics.

observations.label: November 17 04:52 PM EST after-hours observation
observations.value: CRDO approximately +2.46% at $127 (Benzinga); after-hours quote, not a closing price

observations.label: Company announcement
observations.value: Agreement resolving patent rights dispute related to Active Electrical Cable technology and Marvell USPTO challenges; terms confidential

observations.label: Next checks and invalidation
observations.value: Any royalty/license disclosures, customer wins, cable adoption, margins and competing interconnect products; unfavorable terms or share losses weaken interpretation

items.key_finding: An identified intellectual-property uncertainty in AI data-center connectivity has been resolved, with undisclosed economics.

items.title: UKMTO warning 211 reports tanker strike and missing crew member near Khasab
items.summary: UKMTO published a time-delayed report of a tanker struck by an unidentified projectile 13 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman. The onboard fire was extinguished, and search-and-rescue efforts were underway for one missing crew member. The incident's exact time and whether it overlaps earlier reports need reconciliation; no sustained oil-export loss has been verified.

observations.label: UKMTO publication
observations.value: Warning #211 dated 18 Nov 2026; time-delayed incident report; occurrence time not confirmed

observations.label: Reported physical impact
observations.value: Tanker projectile strike 13 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman; onboard fire extinguished; one crew member missing; cargo damage and export losses unverified

observations.label: November 18 early-European intraday oil indication
observations.value: Brent approximately $91.38/bbl (-1.9%) and WTI approximately $83.80/bbl (-2.6%), per WSJ; not settlement prices

observations.label: Next checks and invalidation
observations.value: UKMTO detail and vessel identity versus warnings 208/207, crew status, damage, tanker transits, freight and insurance, EIA inventory at 10:30 AM ET; duplicate incident report or absence of export disruption weakens escalation inference

items.key_finding: Official maritime reporting adds a serious tanker incident, but it does not establish a new sustained oil-flow loss.

sources.title: WSJ November 18 oil inventory and Hormuz coverage

items.title: Nvidia earnings spark broad premarket rebound in AI chips and neoclouds
items.summary: Nvidia's stronger-than-expected revenue outlook lifted semiconductor and AI infrastructure shares in Wednesday premarket trading. Reuters observed Nvidia up 3.7%; WSJ reported stronger moves in CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN. These are preliminary market reactions, not confirmed closes, and debt-heavy infrastructure customers still face financing and deployment risks.

observations.label: Reuters Nov 18 5:28 AM EST premarket
observations.value: NVDA +3.7%; preliminary premarket, not regular-session closing move

observations.label: WSJ Nov 18 morning premarket snapshots
observations.value: CRWV +6.5%, NBIS +8.4%, IREN +7.0%, AMD +3.0%; intraday snapshots, not closing moves

observations.label: Earnings catalyst
observations.value: Nvidia Q4 revenue guidance $130B ±3% versus LSEG analyst consensus $125.25B, issued Nov 17

observations.label: Fundamental assessment and invalidation
observations.value: AI compute demand remains strong; watch financing of neoclouds, GPU utilization, margins and hyperscaler capex; weak cash conversion or market reversal would undermine recovery signal

items.key_finding: Wednesday's premarket rebound broadens Nvidia's earnings relief to indebted AI-infrastructure operators.

sources.title: Reuters November 18 futures and Nvidia reaction
WSJ Nvidia shares lift AI suppliers and neoclouds

items.title: Large API inventory builds coincide with crude-price retreat despite Gulf shipping risk
items.summary: API's preliminary weekly estimates showed sizeable U.S. crude and gasoline inventory builds for the week ended November 13, and crude prices declined in Wednesday's early trading. Gulf tanker threats and a reported Saudi pipeline attack claim have not been tied to independently verified sustained export losses. The official EIA release is the next supply confirmation point.

observations.label: API estimates for week ended Nov 13, published Nov 17
observations.value: US crude +5.3M barrels; gasoline +5.1M; Cushing crude -1.69M; preliminary, not EIA confirmed

observations.label: AP early November 18 crude observation
observations.value: Brent about $91.67/bbl, down 1.6%; early trading, not settlement

observations.label: Physical shipping flow evidence
observations.value: No independently reconciled sustained incremental oil-export loss established; existing UKMTO warnings remain relevant

observations.label: Risks, invalidation and next checks
observations.value: EIA crude/products, refinery throughput, oil exports, UKMTO/MARAD, Saudi pipeline status, tanker/freight stress, Brent/WTI and XLE/XOP; verified disrupted cargo flows would outweigh preliminary inventory build

items.key_finding: Supply-build evidence is pressing crude prices lower while Gulf maritime threats remain a separate, not yet quantified flow risk.
